title: Chapter 1048
paragraphs: Chapter 1048
Episode 250. Zipple and Kinzelo (2)
The Abyss Legion.
They were new troops supported by the witch Orgal, relentlessly attacking Zipple without rest while Vahn and the Plutonian clan were on their mission.
[Hisss, sss!]

As the leading soldier hissed like a snake, the troops scattered. Orgal did not show himself until the dimensional gate closed, but the soldiers, without anyone's command, moved in unison and quickly surrounded Kelliark and Bligiet.
"What do you think, Lord Bligiet? Can you see what these beings truly are?"
Before Kelliark could ask, Bligiet was already intrigued by the Abyss Legion.
The bizarre soldiers raised by the witch Heluram seemed to have lost all will and language, making only hissing noises. Their empty eye sockets held nothing but blind obsession instead of eyeballs.
[Mortals, and among them, those who were once humans. Extremely dangerous and powerful.]
"Ho, interesting..."

Kelliark had already analyzed the Abyss Legion using the Origin Stone. However, the Origin Stone couldn't define what the Abyss Legion was. Not only was it unable to analyze their identity, but it also couldn't manipulate them directly.
For instance, it couldn't make the arm of a black soldier, who was swinging a sword, disappear as if it had never existed. Such manipulations had no effect on them.
Therefore, when Zipple faced the Abyss Legion, he didn’t combat the soldiers themselves but manipulated the environment of the battlefield to counter them.
Just like how he suddenly removed the ground beneath a soldier rushing at him.
[Shriek!]
The charging soldier lost his balance. His sword missed the air in front of Kelliark, who then immediately used a spatial explosion to repel him.

"So, they were mortals deemed worthy of evaluation by Lord Bligiet... Indeed, they are comparable to the current top-class superhumans. They perfectly handle situations where the ground disappears without warning and space explodes."
While Kelliark was speaking, other soldiers were attacking him. Kelliark continued to dodge their attacks by manipulating the environment using the Origin Stone.
"But then it becomes even more incomprehensible. Throughout the history of mortals, there haven't been many who have reached such a level, so how can there be absolutely no information about them..."
Even without relying on the Origin Stone, if, as Bligiet said, the Abyss Legion were mortal beings, some inferences should have been possible.

However, the swordsmanship and magic used by the soldiers were difficult to characterize. In some aspects, they resembled demons, in others, they reminded him of Runcandel or Hairan, and in some ways, they seemed similar to Zipple’s magic.
Even to Bligiet's eyes, no more information was visible beyond the fact that they were mortals. This puzzled him.
[I will help, though it's unrelated to our agreement. I too am curious about what exactly they are. Helluram... must have some dark ulterior motive.]
Bligiet said, spreading his palms. Then, a giant sphere formed in the sky, and solar energy began to pour out in all directions.
The soldiers skillfully fended off the solar energy, but Bligiet felt an indescribable dissonance in their movements.
‘Helluram’s soldiers… seem to have fought against me before.’
Bligiet had just resurrected and hadn't battled anyone other than Vahn. He had no memories of facing such humans in ancient times.
‘Not just once, but several times. Clearly, they know me…!’
Otherwise, the way the Abyss Legion was fighting couldn't be explained. They were attacking in the most troublesome manner for Bligiet.

Some continuously engaged in close combat to prevent him from focusing on his powers, some sought to remove his shield and find hidden sun energy within it, while others anticipated and reacted to his movements.
To Bligiet, it felt as though the Abyss Legion could see right through him.

Even Vahn, considered the strongest mortal in history, couldn’t do this. Moreover, the Abyss Legion seemed to rely purely on experience and instinct, as they showed neither insight nor the slightest bit of rational thought.
It was immensely frustrating. To be figured out by beings that were neither Helluram nor her subordinates, but mere puppets.
The only relief was that, although they were strong, they were not as formidable as Vahn.
If Vahn had known Bligiet this well, he would never have reached the Tower of Story unscathed.
"Lord Bligiet, have you ever encountered these beings before?"

Kelliark too felt that the Abyss Legion knew Bligiet's tactics too well. It wouldn't be strange to consider them as weapons designed specifically against Bligiet. The soldiers attacking Kelliark did not show such signs.
[No.]

Bligiet was suppressing his anger. It was anger born from anxiety. The opponent knew him, but he didn’t know the opponent. As an avatar of the Sun God, Bligiet should never have been in such a situation.
Of course, just because the Abyss Legion knew Bligiet didn’t mean he was at a disadvantage. It was impossible to inflict any essential damage on him unless it was done by Genesis.
“So, these creatures are unpleasant for both Lord Bligiet and us in Zipple. The Abyss Legion is the only one that can ignore the Origin Stone's defense line and enter the tower directly.”
Only because Kelliark had “permitted” it, could Bligiet have reached it.
In Kelliark’s opinion, the current defense line built by the Origin Stone was impervious to any force in the world.
Moreover, the defense line was getting stronger every day, thanks to the Origin Stone, the Holy Land, and Elona harmonizing faster than expected.
While fighting off the incoming Abyss Legion, Bligiet was deep in thought.

‘What Heluram ultimately wants... as far as I know, it's similar to Malugia. Moreover, unlike us, her status hasn’t been seriously compromised. If she wanted, she could start leading the world to destruction at any time. So why is she using such inefficient means?’
The Abyss Legion was shocking, but for Bligiet, there were questions.
If Helluram’s intention was to secure Malugia, or Elona, for her purpose, the most certain way would have been to act personally.
From Bligiet's perspective, the Origin Stone was not yet a weapon that could stand against Helluram, even if it was poison to numerous other mortals and immortals.
Originally, Bligiet considered that there were only two beings in the world who could stand against Heluram: Himself, either complete or nearly complete, and Solderet.

‘Now that I think about it, Solderet’s power is only faintly remaining in the Jin Runcandel and his guardian dragon. There is something I don’t know. Once Airan's constraint is lifted, I must meet Helluram.’
Chiiing-!

A streak of solar energy finally severed the neck of a black soldier. The decapitated soldier stopped moving like a corpse and then dispersed into particles. These particles flowed into a small steel dimensional gate formed nearby.
[These creatures do not die. Their scattered bodies will return to the one who sent them. But that is not Helluram.]
“Then who is it?”
[A person blessed by Helluram. That person is commanding the Abyss Legion.]
At the same time, in Orgal’s subspace.

Orgal watched the particles escaping through a small steel dimensional gate. The particles wriggled like bugs before clumping together like black jewels. Watching this, he couldn’t hide his troubled mind.
It wasn’t that he was upset about the destruction of an Abyss Legion soldier. After all, the soldier would recover on its own after some time and return to the battlefield.

There were already dozens of such soldiers. Soon there would be hundreds, then thousands, hundreds of thousands, millions… Orgal couldn’t predict how many there would be. Even the witch said she couldn't remember all their numbers.
In a way, Kinzelo had obtained its greatest power since its foundation.
Whether it was the support received by Jo to create a true Plutonian clan or the gathering of the strong from the Demon World or the executive repeatedly training and fighting to become stronger.
None of these could compare to the Abyss Legion given by Helluram. If Helluram had given the Abyss Legion without any cost, and had sent them without revealing any truth.
Kinzelo might have finally achieved its grand ambition. They might have finally changed the world into the correct form they desired.
[Damn it…]
But Orgal was not happy.

The truth revealed by his old lover was that this world was dirtier, more complex, more cruel, and more dangerous than he had imagined. Therefore, the Abyss Legion could not be used for Kinzelo, for the resurrection of the Sun God.
[Damn, why, how... Damn it!]
Even Bubar and Ainas (Kinzelo had just moved to this subspace right after Orgal returned) were too oppressed by his rage to utter their usual foolish words.
While Orgal was incessantly pulling his hair, his gaze remained fixed on the black lump that the soldier had transformed into.
“Leader, you need to stay strong.”
It was Marjiella. Her wheelchair stopped next to Orgal, and Zephrin approached and spoke.
“Master, the witch's words may not be true. Then there is still hope for us…”
[No… Zephrin, Heluram’s words are probably true. I can feel it. Only I can feel it. This black lump… it's me. Really me…]
-These are your failed selves.
-Or perhaps, the failed selves of your world, Orgal.
As the members sighed and hung their heads, Orgal recalled Heluram’s words. That terrible story.
